quote: We design automatic evaluation methods in three dimensions: fluency, correctness, and citation quality. Specifically, we use MAUVE to measure fluency, propose tailored correctness metrics for each dataset, and adopt a natural language inference (NLI) model to measure citation quality.

We design automatic evaluation methods in three dimensions: fluency, correctness, and citation quality. Specifically, we use MAUVE to measure fluency, propose tailored correctness metrics for each dataset, and adopt a natural language inference (NLI) model to measure citation quality.

We conduct human evaluation ( §6) to demonstrate strong correlation with our automatic metrics.
guideline: Workers rate utility (1-5 score), judge citation recall (whether cited passages fully support statements), and citation precision (whether citations fully/partially support statements).
Workers rate utility on a Likert scale and assess citation recall and citation precision for each statement and its citations.

workers to judge model generations on three dimensions: (1) utility: a 1-to-5 score indicating whether the generation helps answer the question; (2) citation recall: judge whether the passages fully support the sentence; (3) citation precision: judge whether the citation 'fully supports', 'partially supports', or 'does not support' the sentence.
